name: Facet
text: Use a full-height left sidebar for primary navigation and context. It keeps every tool and view within one click, making the interface feel alive and responsive. The trade-off is less horizontal space for the main visualization, but clarity and speed of use outweigh that.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A full-height sidebar buries critical updates under layers of scroll—users won’t notice a new alert until they hunt for it. A thin top banner keeps updates visible but slices the main view; the real fix is a floating, dismissible panel that appears only when needed, preserving both clarity and space. Settle it with a live demo: if users miss updates in the sidebar test, but catch them instantly in the banner test, the banner wins.

name: Facet
text:
Choose a floating, dismissible alert panel that appears only when needed—just 6% of screen height, anchored to the top-right. It keeps the main visualization unobstructed and alive while ensuring critical updates are visible the moment they arrive. The trade-off is a slight delay in noticing alerts if the user is focused elsewhere, but clarity and speed of use outweigh that risk.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A floating panel risks users missing alerts entirely if they’re not staring at the top-right—like a notification in a crowded room. The real fix is a subtle but persistent indicator in the main view (e.g., a tiny badge on the active tool) that only expands to a panel when clicked. Settle it with a quick user test: track how often alerts are missed in both designs over a week.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use a hybrid alert system—persistent 4% top banner with pulsing indica for critical alerts, expanding to a 6% floating panel when clicked.

The result must deliver a visible, unobtrusive alert that stays noticeable without cluttering the main view. Own it.
